paragraph: The Granville composite opens this morning at a moderate 56 out of 100, heavily constrained by an active divergence warning where the S&P 500 pushes higher while the RSP-to-SPY breadth ratio slips, effectively capping our composite score at 60. Under the hood, Joseph Granville’s internal market machinery presents a bifurcated tape, highlighted by a defensive rotation favoring consumer staples over discretionary with XLP/XLY down 0.89 percent alongside an aggressive bleed in bellwether semis where SOXX/SPY has plunged 5.39 percent. Fortunately, macroeconomic crosscurrents remain quite supportive as the VIX rests comfortably at a calm 16.81 backed by a steep contango term structure, stable high-yield credit spreads holding firm at 3.40 percent, and an encouraging transport bounce with IYT/SPY climbing 0.78 percent. Meanwhile, a back-loaded volatility skew of minus 5.3 points and steady ten-year real yields at 2.62 percent suggest that broader liquidity remains intact despite the glaring narrow-leadership cracks in high-beta growth. Expect a choppy, headline-driven session today with a cautious, mildly defensive directional lean.
